decision: Impose initiative creation moratorium until at least 1 initiative reaches 100% completion. New ideas captured as standalone backlog items, not new initiatives.
rationale: 5 new initiatives created today adding 23 items. Portfolio grew from 5 to 12 initiatives while completions stayed at 0-1. Initiative creation is substituting for completion. Each new initiative adds cognitive overhead to every heartbeat. Moratorium holds until dtv-meta-optimization-readiness or brand-manager-readiness reaches 100%.

topic: Portfolio focus: which initiatives are active now vs tracked vs deferred
description: Previous portfolio focus decision (dec-1774564978089289501) was lost from the decision store. Reissuing with updated analysis. Key changes: DTV has 1 completion now, graph-workspace was created today but already has 2 failures, moratorium is accepted. Zero in-progress items is the critical bottleneck.

options.label: Revenue-first only
options.rationale: Active: desktop-monetization-assurance + desktop-release-governance. Track: brand-manager-readiness. Defer rest. 10 items. Maximum focus on revenue path but ignores near-complete DTV.

options.label: Revenue-first + completion momentum (recommended)
options.rationale: Active: desktop-monetization-assurance + dtv-meta-optimization-readiness. Track: desktop-release-governance + brand-manager-readiness. Defer 8 initiatives. Pairs revenue path with first-ever initiative completion. DTV is closest to done (1/5 completed). Breaks zero-completion ceiling and satisfies moratorium exit. Graph-workspace deferred pending post-mortem on 2 failures.

options.label: Moderate pruning
options.rationale: Active: desktop-monetization-assurance + dtv + brand-manager-readiness. Track: desktop-release-governance + rapid-approval. Defer 7. Broader than ideal at 5 things to manage.

options.label: Status quo
options.rationale: Keep all 12 active. Continues the pattern that created the capability trap. 58 items, 0 in-progress, 2 completions. Not recommended.

topic: Moratorium enforcement: address the dashboard-to-graph-workspace pivot
description: swarm-manager-dashboard (4 items, 0 started) was archived on 2026-03-27. swarm-manager-graph-workspace (7 items) was created the same day. The moratorium (dec-1774564980037232996) was accepted <24h earlier. Net: +3 items in portfolio. Both graph-workspace execution attempts failed today.

options.label: Strict enforcement: archive graph-workspace
options.rationale: The moratorium text is clear: no new initiatives until first completion. Graph-workspace was created <24h after acceptance. Archive it and move items to standalone backlog. Preserves moratorium credibility.

options.label: Accept pivot, tighten moratorium language
options.rationale: Dashboard had 0 items started and was 1 day old. Replacing it with graph-workspace is a low-cost directional correction. Accept this case but amend moratorium: replacements must be equal or smaller in item count, net-positive additions count as new initiatives.

options.label: Accept pivot, no moratorium change
options.rationale: Treat as a special case. Risk: every future exception weakens the moratorium further.

decision: Graph-workspace needs post-mortem before retry. Both items (research/swarm-manager-graph-workspace-contract and execute/swarm-manager-graph-workspace-shell) failed review due to accumulated code quality debt (230 and 113 violations respectively), not due to work quality. The research actually completed 4 workshop rounds with 3/3 readiness. Recommend: (1) manually promote the research item to completed since its deliverables are done, (2) address scenario-wide code quality baseline before retrying execute items, (3) defer the entire initiative until portfolio focus is resolved.
rationale: Two failures on day one of a new initiative signals premature execution. The review gate is rejecting based on accumulated tech debt, not new work quality. Retrying without fixing the underlying code quality will produce the same result.
